# Generated files

This page lists the files `Generate` writes, when it refuses to write them, and the modules the generated code imports, for a developer wiring wiregen's output into a TypeScript build.

## What Generate writes

`Registry.Generate(ctx, opts...)` writes these files under `WithTSDir`, by the names the options set, plus the OpenAPI document at each path `WithOpenAPIFiles` names:

| File | Written when |
| --- | --- |
| `types.gen.ts` | always |
| `decoders.gen.ts` | always |
| `validators.gen.ts` | always |
| `events.gen.ts` | `Events` is non-empty |
| `constants.gen.ts` | `Constants` is non-empty |
| `client.gen.ts` | `Endpoints` is non-empty, see [Typed HTTP client](http-client.md) |
| the arbitraries module | `WithArbitrariesFile` is set, see [Property-test arbitraries](arbitraries.md) |
| the OpenAPI document | `WithOpenAPIFiles` is set, with the same bytes at every path it names |
| `deadset-edges.json` | `WithDeadsetEdges` is set, at the target root it names, see [Deadset edges file](#deadset-edges-file) |

Every TypeScript file starts with the header comment, `// Code generated by wiregen. DO NOT EDIT.` unless `WithHeaderComment` changes it. The output is byte-identical from run to run.

## Errors and writing

`Generate` builds every file in memory first, and returns an error and writes nothing when:

- the `Registry` or the context is nil, `WithTSDir` is missing, or `WithTransportImport` is missing while endpoints are registered.
- a type or enum is registered with no package or name, twice, or under a bare name another package's type also takes.
- two enums emit the same TypeScript type name or value-array name, or an enum cannot be resolved (see [Enums](type-mapping.md#enums)).
- a registered type is not a struct or a map, or a field cannot cross the wire with a checked shape (see [What Generate refuses](type-mapping.md#what-generate-refuses)).
- a union does not fit its type (see [Unions](type-mapping.md#unions)).
- an event has no name, a name with a line break, no data type, or a name used twice.
- two generated names collide in the modules' shared namespace (see [Identifiers](type-mapping.md#identifiers)).
- a TypeScript output is absolute or leaves the TS directory, by its path or through a symlink, or two outputs, TypeScript or OpenAPI, are one file: from some file or directory on both paths, compared by device and inode once its symlinks are followed, the same names below it, compared without case, whether or not the file exists yet.
- a `Const`'s `TSName` has no characters left once cleaned to an identifier.
- the endpoint table is invalid (see [Validation](http-client.md#validation)), names a security scheme `OpenAPI.SecuritySchemes` does not declare or lists an empty or repeated role, has a server with no URL, a server URL that is not valid UTF-8 or holds outside its placeholders a query, fragment, space, control character, double quote, any of `` <>\^`| `` or a `%` that starts no percent-encoding, a variable value holding one or a brace, a malformed or repeated placeholder, a `{name}` no variable defines, a variable its URL does not use, or a variable with no `Default` or a `Default` outside its `Enum`, or a scheme is malformed.
- a mapping has no `TS`.
- a `TSNameOverride`, `PathNameOverride` or `EnumTSNameOverride` key names no registered type or enum, or a `Mappings` key is reached by no registered type's field.
- OpenAPI files are named without `OpenAPI.Title` and `Version`, an OpenAPI path climbs with `..` out of a directory that does not exist, a mapping has no `Schema`, two components would share a name, or a `$ref` in the document is not a string or names nothing in it.
- the TS directory lies outside the `WithDeadsetEdges` target root, or the existing edges file is not a valid edges document or holds a hand-written edge under `wiregen/`, as [Deadset edges file](#deadset-edges-file) describes.
- the registered packages fail to load or type-check.

Every error that lists fields lists all of them, so one run reports every fix.

Each file, the OpenAPI documents included, is then staged with [filesafe](https://github.com/cplieger/go/tree/main/filesafe) as a temporary file beside its target, creating any missing parent directory as `os.MkdirAll` does, with the mode the umask leaves, and only once every file is staged is each committed: synced, renamed into place and its directory synced. A staging failure, such as a full disk, an unwritable directory or a target that is not a regular file, leaves every target untouched and no temporary file behind, though a parent directory it created stays. Each commit is atomic, but the commits run one after another, so a failure partway through them can leave some files new and others old.

`ctx` bounds the package load, which runs the `go` command as a subprocess. Cancelling it stops the pass, and the cancellation reason, including a cause set with `context.WithCancelCause`, is reachable with `errors.Is`.

## Validators module

The decoders import their checks by name from `validators.gen.ts`, which wiregen writes on every run, so it always matches the decoders and you never edit it. Your own hand-written decoders may import and build on the same helpers.

A failed check throws a `TypeError` whose message starts with the JSON path, such as `$.user.id: expected number, got string`. `decodeArray` and `decodeRecord` add the element index or key to the path. The module exports:

- `type Decoder<T> = (v: unknown) => T`
- `own(o: globalThis.Record<string, unknown>, key: string): unknown`, reading only an own property, so an inherited `constructor` or `toString` reads as `undefined`
- `asObject(v: unknown, path = "$"): globalThis.Record<string, unknown>`
- `asArray(v: unknown, path = "$"): unknown[]`
- `reqStr`, `reqNum` and `reqBool(o: globalThis.Record<string, unknown>, key: string, path = "$")`, where `reqNum` rejects `NaN` and `Infinity`
- `optStr`, `optNum` and `optBool(o, key, path = "$")`, returning `undefined` for an absent key, for hand-written decoders
- `reqOneOf<T extends string>(o, key, vals: readonly T[], path = "$"): T`
- `decodeArray<T>(v: unknown, decode: Decoder<T>, path = "$"): T[]`
- `decodeRecord<T>(v: unknown, decode: Decoder<T>, path = "$"): globalThis.Record<string, T>`, whose every key, `__proto__` included, is an own property
- `refuseKeys(o, keys: readonly string[], path = "$"): void`, which refuses a present, non-null value at any of `keys`
- `checkRange(v: number, lo, hi, path = "$")`, `checkBytes(s: string, max, path = "$")`, `checkPattern(s: string, pattern, path = "$")` and `checkCount(a: T[], lo, hi, path = "$")`, each returning its value or throwing

## Events module

With `Events` registered, `events.gen.ts` exports:

- `type EventFrame`, the union of `{event: "<name>", data: <Type>}` over every event.
- `type EventName`, the union of the event names.
- `EVENT_DECODERS`, one decoder per event name.
- `decodeEventFrame(event: string, data: unknown): EventFrame`, which decodes one frame and throws on an unknown name.

Your event-stream code reads each `EventSource` message's `event` and parsed `data` and passes them to `decodeEventFrame`. No module of yours is imported.

## Deadset edges file

[deadset](https://github.com/cplieger/deadset) finds unused code across Go and TypeScript. A Go wire type that only the generated TypeScript reads looks unused to it. An [edges document](https://github.com/cplieger/deadset-spec/blob/dev/docs/edges.md) declares that use, and `WithDeadsetEdges(targetRoot)` writes one for everything wiregen generates.

Pass the directory deadset analyses, relative to the working directory. wiregen writes `deadset-edges.json` there, the one name and place deadset reads. The TS directory must lie below it.

```go
err := r.Generate(ctx, wiregen.WithTSDir("web/src/wire"), wiregen.WithDeadsetEdges("."))
```

Each edge pairs a Go symbol with the TypeScript symbol generated from it.

| Go symbol | TypeScript symbol | Identifier |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a registered struct, named map or union | its type in the types file | `wiregen/<Type>` |
| a field of a registered struct, not a union | the property in the types file, by its wire name | `wiregen/<Type>/<Field>` |
| an enum type | its type in the types file | `wiregen/<Enum>` |
| an enum constant | the enum's value array in the decoders file, or the enum's type when no decoder reads the enum | `wiregen/<Enum>/<Const>` |

A field promoted from an embedded struct is paired as that struct's field, such as `Base.ID`, and its identifier keeps the dot, as in `wiregen/User/Base.ID`. Each Go name rune outside ASCII is written as `-u` and six hex digits in the identifier. A `Const` has no Go symbol, and endpoints and events are strings, so none of them gets an edge.

The TypeScript side names its package the way deadset does. wiregen walks up from the generated file to the target root, and the first `package.json` with a `name` gives `ts://<name>/<path below that package.json>`. With none, the side reads `ts://./<path below the target root>`. A Go package whose files lie outside the target root gets no edges, because deadset cannot see it.

Every generated edge has `"because": "generated by wiregen"`. When the file exists, wiregen keeps its `description` and every edge outside `wiregen/` as written, and replaces every edge under `wiregen/`. A removed type therefore loses its edges, and running again without changes writes the same bytes.

Generate refuses, naming each identifier, an edge under `wiregen/` without that `because`, so a hand-written edge is never deleted. Rename such an edge outside the prefix. Generate also refuses a file that deadset would refuse. Such a file is larger than 1 MiB, is not JSON, or holds a duplicate key or a member other than `description` and `edges`.

The file is written with the other outputs, keys sorted, two-space indents and a trailing newline. Commit it, and check in CI that regenerating leaves it unchanged, so a stale edge fails before deadset reports it.
